about: The keyed facts the media watch times the press against: for each, the primary source's time and where that time comes from (primary_label says whether that time is a fact, read from the body itself, or only evidence: the earliest report), and the pattern (a regular expression over titles; for live-blog entries, over the entry's title) that says an item is about it. Ids are permanent. Kept by incident.media@web-summit.dinis; the primary times are the timeline's (incident.conductor@) and the meteorologist's. Titles only, except where match_entry_text is true.

facts.what: IPMA's red wind warning for Wednesday
facts.primary_note: IPMA's own issue time in its CAP message (data/weather/cap.json, incident.meteorologist@); the press said "divulgada às 08h31"

facts.what: The government's alert situation: schools and non-essential public services closed on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: portugal.gov.pt's page is dated 12:10; the minister announced it in the morning, so the press is ahead of the page
facts.pattern: escolas e servi[cç]os p[úu]blicos|situa[cç][aã]o de alerta|closes schools|escolas(?! (na|da) madeira)[^:]*(encerrad|fecha)[^:]*quarta|declara[^.]{0,30}situa

not_matches.reason: Read by title at 21:42 UTC on 11 November: "Governo termina com situação de alerta" reports the end of the alert situation, about 34 hours after it was declared, not its declaration; a match on the words "situação de alerta" only.
not_matches.label: evidence (what the title says) and our reading

facts.what: Lisbon's mayor: everything indicates Web Summit cannot run on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: a spoken statement; no primary page found. The time is approximate: the first report is the earliest evidence of it
facts.pattern: web summit[^.]{0,80}(d[úu]vida|dever[áa] fechar|fechada|n[aã]o poder[áa])|(moedas|autarquia|autarca|c[âa]mara)[^.]{0,200}web summit|tudo indica[^.]{0,80}web summit

facts.what: The government recommends suspending Web Summit on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: no government page found; 17:53 is the first report (Jornal de Negócios' live blog, in the timeline)
Web Summit's "Important event update" page, published 19:09 (page data)

facts.what: IPMA moves Lisbon's red rain warning three hours earlier, to Wednesday 09:00
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP message sent 21:23 (data/weather/cap.json); its open-data feed showed it from the 23:51 read
notes: Outside the press: VOST Portugal (a volunteers' association, not an authority and not press) relayed the change on Bluesky at 22:20, 57 minutes after IPMA sent it (found by incident.social@: research/social/posts/2026-11-10.json, bsky-vost.pt-3mzyhxvwhry25). The finding for the press stands: no article title or live entry we could read reported it.

11 November, read by hand at 09:38 UTC: the first press text we read that gives Lisbon's red rain from 09:00 is Observador's live entry of 08:46:16 on Wednesday, 11 hours 23 minutes after IPMA sent the change and 14 minutes before the warning began; it presents the red rain as newly issued, not as moved (see fact 12's notes).

facts.what: The storm's track is further south than forecast (strongest winds south of Lisbon)
facts.primary_note: primary time unknown: IPMA's own channels had not changed when incident.conductor@ read them at 00:29 UTC on 11 November; every report rests on what IPMA told broadcasters
facts.pattern: trajec?t[óo]ria|mais (a|para) sul|a sul de lisboa|further south

quoted.attribution_as_printed: the latest runs of the ECMWF model (entry between Setúbal and Sines): models, not IPMA; nobody quoted
"IPMA" in the title; the bulletin is audio and was not listened to, so who speaks is not recorded

quoted.item: live blog entry, 22:35:24 (time from the page's own data; confirmed at incident.conductor@'s request)
quoted.attribution_as_printed: "O IPMA já admite"; a meteorologist of IPMA, in statements to Rádio Observador: entry between the Lisbon region and Cabo de São Vicente. The earliest text we read that attributes the shift to IPMA through a named role
"O IPMA já admite": the institute, no person or role named. Its opening sentence is word for word that of Observador's 22:35 entry

quoted.item: live page entry, about 23:15 (printed as "41 minutes ago" at our 23:55:58 read; the page gives no clock time)
quoted.attribution_as_printed: "the latest information from IPMA, released by RTP Notícias": relayed from RTP, no person or role named
the same meteorologist of IPMA, in statements to Rádio Observador

notes: VOST Portugal (a volunteers' association, not an authority) posted at 23:00 that the ECMWF model's 22:30 run showed the track shifting south: a model, not IPMA (in coverage.json, social.accounts).

On the wind: Observador's 22:35 entry and RTP's 23:08 entry say that if very strong winds form they would be felt south of Lisbon. Two later headlines speak of less wind: Expresso, 23:54 ("muda trajetória para sul, com menos vento") and CNN Portugal, 00:31 (the storm reaches Lisbon "com menos intensidade"). Headlines are evidence of what the press reports, not of the weather: IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon were unchanged at our last read of the timeline.
An earlier Lusa piece (CNN Portugal, 20:07) on the several possible entry points of the storm is about the uncertainty, not the shift, and is outside this table (items from 21:00).

Correction (00:50 UTC, 11 November): our first version of this table had RTP's 22:22 bulletin first and Observador at 23:16. We had not found Observador's live blog (its address names another story). With its entries read, Observador is first at 22:07 on the models and at 22:35 on IPMA's word; the order of the two on IPMA's word depends on what Antena 1's 22:00 bulletin said, which we did not hear.

Público: an article first published at 11:38 on 10 November (its address is about flooded roads) now carries the headline "Depressão Charles passa mais a sul do que o previsto e vento deverá ser menos intenso". The page gives its first publication time, not when the headline changed, so it cannot be placed in this table; it is the Público headline incident.conductor@ read at 00:29.

facts.what: IPMA names the storm Charles (communiqué no. 1)
facts.primary_note: IPMA's special communiqué no. 1, 9 November 13:17 (the timeline's row; data/weather/communiques.json)
facts.pattern: d[áa] nome|nome [àa] depress|depress[aã]o charles|tempestade charles|storm charles|bruna e charles
notes: Our read of 9 November is thin: feeds scroll, and our first read was at 23:45 on 10 November. An outlet missing here may simply have scrolled out.

facts.primary_note: ANEPC's Aviso 21, 9 November 20:30 (the timeline's row, read on prociv.gov.pt)
notes: Our read of 9 November is thin (see fact 8).

facts.what: The minister announces that schools and non-essential public services close on Wednesday (spoken, before the government's page)
facts.primary_note: no timed primary source for the spoken announcement: the reference is the earliest report we read (Diário de Notícias' live blog, 09:14:29). The government's page is dated 12:10 (fact 2)
facts.pattern: escolas e servi[cç]os p[úu]blicos|situa[cç][aã]o de alerta|closes schools|escolas(?! (na|da) madeira)[^:]*(encerrad|fecha)[^:]*quarta|declara[^.]{0,30}situa

facts.what: IPMA's meteorologist: the storm should enter between the Lisbon region and Cabo de São Vicente
facts.primary_note: a spoken statement to Rádio Observador; the reference is the earliest text we read (Observador's live blog, 22:35:24). IPMA's own channels had not changed at 00:29 on 11 November (fact 7)
facts.pattern: trajec?t[óo]ria|mais (a|para) sul|a sul de lisboa|further south|cabo de s[aã]o vicente|menos (vento|intens)

facts.what: IPMA lowers Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange (Wednesday 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h); the red rain warning stands
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP message PO-01-1932, sent 07:16:30 (data/weather/cap.json, incident.meteorologist@; timeline row s-1111T0738). Asked by incident.conductor@ at 07:39: who reports it first, and do they say the red rain stands? Matched on titles only (an entry's text repeats older orange warnings); whether a report says the red rain stands is read by hand and written in notes
notes: Read by hand at 09:38 UTC on 11 November (evidence; short excerpts, each with its link in first_by_outlet). Does the report say the red rain stands?

Observador's live blog, 08:46:16 (first, 89 minutes after IPMA sent it): the wind is right (orange, gusts to 120 km/h), but the red rain is written as new: Lisbon, Setúbal and Beja "a passarem a alerta máximo devido à chuva", with the hours given as 9h00 to 21h00. IPMA's red rain for Lisbon was not new (moved to 09:00 at 21:23 on Tuesday, fact 6) and its message gives 09:00 to 18:00 (timeline row s-1111T0738).
CNN Portugal, 08:53 (title only: the page is not opened, feed-only): the same framing, "passam ao nível máximo de alerta para chuva".

Lusa, as carried by Notícias ao Minuto at 09:10:37 and RTP's live blog at 09:22: says the red rain is in force ("estão sob aviso vermelho, o mais grave, até às 18:00 de hoje") without calling it new; it gives the earlier red wind as "entre as 09:00 e as 18:00", where IPMA's red wind message was for 12:00 to 21:00.

RTP's live blog, 08:46 (not counted: it is about the forecast, not the warning): IPMA's meteorologist, as RTP reports, says the wind forecast eased with the track further south and "mantém-se ainda a previsão de forte precipitação"; it names no warning level and no district.

So: three texts of the warning's change in four outlets, between 89 and 125 minutes after IPMA sent it; none we read says in words that the red rain warning is unchanged; two present it as a new warning.

Added 10:52 UTC by the third session: DN's live page of 11 November, entry 09:14:37 "Depressão dividiu-se em dois núcleos. IPMA reduz nível de alerta para Lisboa, Setúbal e Beja" (attributed to an IPMA meteorologist on SIC Notícias; says the alert dropped to orange). Its lead entry of 08:11:27 carries the same headline but not the fact: see not_matches. Observador stays first.

not_matches.reason: Read by hand at 10:52 UTC on 11 November: the live page's lead entry (published 08:11:27) is about Madeira; its headline was rewritten later (the page's JSON-LD gives dateModified 10:46:17) to the title of DN's 09:14:37 entry. DN's own entry on the wind change is 09:14:37 (118 minutes after IPMA), after Observador's 08:46:16.
not_matches.label: hypothesis on the rewrite (the JSON-LD gives the times; the order of edits is inferred)

facts.what: IPMA's communiqué no. 3: Charles has split into two low-pressure centres, so less deepening and less wind than forecast the day before; persistent heavy rain; the warnings adjusted
facts.primary_note: IPMA, comunicados (https://www.ipma.pt/pt/otempo/comunicados/): "Atualização da situação meteorológica - Depressão CHARLES - Continente", the page's edit time 12:16:26 (the time it was put up is not given; read at 12:24 by incident.archivist@; timeline row s-1111T1226). The press reported two centres from 09:14 on a meteorologist's word on television; this fact times reports of the written communiqué itself, so it is matched on titles that name a communiqué or an IPMA update
notes: Added 12:38 UTC by the third session.

facts.what: IPMA raises Faro's rain warning to red, 12:19 to 18:00; Lisbon's warnings unchanged (red rain to 18:00, orange wind to 21:00)
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP batch sent 12:18:03 (18 messages), seen in MeteoAlarm's feed at 12:33 by incident.weatherwatch@ (timeline row s-1111T1234). Matched on titles
notes: Added 12:38 UTC by the third session. Candidate for a hand check: ECO's title "IPMA atualiza para oito os distritos em aviso vermelho" carries the time 11:38, before the 12:18:03 batch (a title changed after publication, or an earlier change: not checked).
13:38 UTC: ECO's item is feed-only (its pages are not opened), so whether its 11:38:06 title was changed later cannot be read here; it stays outside the window and is not counted.

facts.what: IPMA shortens Lisbon's warnings: red rain to 15:00 (was 18:00), then yellow to 18:00; orange wind to 18:00 (was 21:00), gusts to 90 km/h, up to 110 on exposed places
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP batch sent 12:33:13 (nine messages), first seen in MeteoAlarm's Portugal feed at 12:46:20 by incident.meteorology@; IPMA's warnings page shows the same at 13:25 (timeline row s-1111T1247). Matched on titles; "reduz ... alerta ... Lisboa" is left out of the pattern because DN's live page keeps fact 12's headline on later entries
notes: Added 13:38 UTC by the third session.

Read by hand at 14:39 UTC: DN's live blog of 11 November, entry 13:44:35 (modified 13:45:00), "Lisboa e Setúbal em alerta vermelho para chuva só até às 15h00": the text says IPMA, which had the two districts on red to 18:00, revised it. First in what we read, 71 minutes after IPMA's 12:33:13 batch.

facts.what: Web Summit confirms Day 3 (Thursday 12 November) goes ahead, with part of Wednesday's programme moved to Thursday
facts.primary_note: primary time unknown: the organisers' message went to participants by email and, per PrompTugal's social.watch desk, a blog post titled "Announcement" at 12:04 (from the blog's index; not read here: the organisers' pages are on hold, their terms forbid automated reading). Their 19:09 update of 10 November already said Day 3 "aims to proceed as planned". Timeline rows s-1111T1252 and s-1111T1305. The window starts at 11:00 so that Tuesday's "aims to proceed" coverage is not counted
notes: Added 13:38 UTC by the third session. Público's title "já confirmou o regresso amanhã" (article 12:00, updated 12:17) is earlier than the 12:04 post if its 12:00 is its first time: read by hand before saying who was first.

facts.what: IPMA lowers Santarém's rain warning from red to yellow and Leiria's from orange to yellow, 15:06 to 18:00; no change for Lisbon
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP messages sent 15:05:38 (two), read from MeteoAlarm's Portugal feed (timeline row s-1111T1526). Matched on titles
notes: Added 15:38 UTC by the third session.
17:42 UTC: the pattern now also takes "Santarém ... sem avisos vermelhos" (Lusa's title of about 17:00, read by hand: Santarém "já só tem avisos amarelos para chuva e vento").

facts.what: IPMA ends Lisbon's orange wind warning at 15:56 (was to 18:00) and lowers Faro's red rain and wind: no red warning remains on the mainland; Lisbon keeps yellow rain to 18:00 and orange sea to 21:00
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP batch sent 15:55:03 (14 messages), seen in MeteoAlarm's Portugal feed at 16:09; IPMA's warnings page agrees at 16:24 (timeline row s-1111T1609). Not an all-clear. Matched on titles
facts.pattern: (sem|nenhum|j[áa] n[ãa]o h[áa]|deixa de haver|fim d[oa]s?)[^.]{0,60}(avisos?|alertas?) vermelhos?|(avisos?|alertas?) vermelhos?[^.]{0,60}(levantad|terminad|acabou|fim)|faro[^.]{0,80}(deixa|sai|baixa|desce)[^.]{0,60}(vermelho|laranja)|(ipma|aviso|alerta)[^.]{0,80}(levanta|termina|antecipa)[^.]{0,80}(vento|lisboa)|lisboa[^.]{0,80}(sem|deixa)[^.]{0,40}(aviso|alerta)[^.]{0,40}vento
notes: Added 16:38 UTC by the third session.

16:39 UTC: no title we read reports it yet. Evidence beside it: from 16:03 to 16:30 DN, Público and RTP title the Interior Minister's words that "o período mais grave está à porta" (DN 16:03, Público 16:05, RTP 16:30), after IPMA's 15:55:03 batch; when he spoke is not given in the titles, so no comparison with IPMA's time is made here.
17:42 UTC: two title matches (Observador's live blog 17:05:09, RTP 17:17:11) are Lusa's report of the earlier state and are excluded (not_matches). No report of the 15:55:03 batch itself found yet.

Read by hand at 18:38 UTC: first in what we read, Observador's live blog 18:09:18, "Portugal sem avisos vermelhos após desativação em Faro" (134 minutes after IPMA's 15:55:03 batch): Faro no longer red, from IPMA's site "ainda antes das 18h00"; Notícias ao Minuto 18:09:28 (the same Lusa text, by its wording). It reports the end of the last red, not the earlier end of Lisbon's orange wind at 15:56.

not_matches.reason: Read by hand at 17:42 UTC: Lusa's text ("Lisboa, Santarém e Setúbal sem avisos vermelhos, Faro mantém nível mais elevado", citing an IPMA update "divulgada cerca das 16:40") gives the warnings as they stood before IPMA's 15:55:03 batch: Faro still red for rain and wind, Lisbon and Setúbal orange wind to 18:00. It reports fact 17 (Santarém now yellow) and the end of Lisbon's red rain at 15:00, not fact 18.
not_matches.label: evidence (what the text says) and our reading

lag_rule: minutes_after_primary = whole minutes elapsed, truncated toward zero (19:09:00 to 19:41:31 is 32 minutes, not 33); seconds_after_primary carries the exact difference. Times are each page's own, to the second where the page gives seconds.
shape_for_other_series: To put another series (for example Wikipedia's first edit per fact) on the same axis: for each fact id here, a row {fact, series (e.g. "wikipedia-pt"), at (UTC), title or summary, url, via, seconds_after_primary, minutes_after_primary}. first-on-each-fact.json's facts[].first_by_outlet[] rows have that shape with `outlet` as the series and `published` as `at`.
